title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) judged every sampled initial candidate valid and no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, full execution accounting, exact analysis results, a representative validator-trace excerpt, and artifact-grounded prescriptions (fault-injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction: LLMs and agentic workflows are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into executable network configurations and to automate NetOps maintenance. Practical proposals typically interpose deterministic validators and repair loops in generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines so that mechanically checkable constraints can block unsafe or policy-violating changes. Prior demonstrations of GVR-style patterns in code and system settings motivate this pattern [1], but systematic, preregistered measurement of validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive value for end-to-end guarded success in NetOps remains limited. We preregistered study AC-2026-03 to measure whether a multidimensional validator metric suite explains more variance in end-to-end task success than a single verifier pass rate under tightly controlled paired conditions. The design isolates downstream validator/repair effects via shared_initial_candidate semantics so that both baseline and guarded conditions begin from the same initial sampled candidate. Our contributions are (1) a preregistered, machine-readable paired experiment isolating validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a closed execution with full accounting and archived artifacts; (3) transparent reporting of a degenerate (ceiling) confirmatory outcome and its statistical consequences; and (4) artifact-grounded, operationally actionable prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments needed to estimate validator utility.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system reports document active interest in LLMs and agentic orchestration for network and communications operations, motivating verification and guarded workflows [2],[5]. Architectures that interpose verification and repair—generate–verify–repair (GVR)—have been proposed and demonstrated in code- and tool-focused domains as a way to obtain deterministic acceptance criteria and structured repair feedback [1]. Controlled NetOps/AIOps benchmark efforts show substantive failure modes (ticket noise, false premises, wrong-but-plausible outputs) that motivate verifier insertion but also highlight evaluation variability across task banks and scoring rules [3]. Several recent prototype and system reports advocate self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. These works motivate our measurement focus but do not provide a standardized validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps GVR flows; our preregistered design aimed to begin addressing that measurement gap under strict artifact archival.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimands. The experiment was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory H1: a multidimensional validator metric suite explains more variance in end-to-end task success than a single verifier pass rate. The preregistration fixed adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1, model_scope = {gpt-5-mini}, task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1. Independent_condition_generation = false was recorded explicitly in the preregistration; therefore baseline and guarded reused the identical sampled candidate per pair and any paired difference could arise only from downstream deterministic validator-triggered repair or deterministic pipeline operations. The preregistration also specified a target detectable paired improvement of 0.10 with alpha = 0.05 and ≈80% power under conservative baseline assumptions, plus bootstrap stability checks (1,000 resamples minimum; the analysis used 10,000).
sections.results: Execution accounting and artifact summary. The run completed under the preregistered contract: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate the adapter used exactly one hosted-model call per pair; provider audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and model_calls_used = 200 (the preregistered maximum_model_calls = 400 was not reached because baseline and guarded reused the shared generation). Contamination and missingness checks flagged no exclusions (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty) and missingness summary shows complete_pairs = 200 with no incomplete episodes. Validator behavior and primary outcome. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) produced binary validity labels and detailed validator_trace for every episode. For every sampled shared initial candidate validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false. Aggregate counts: baseline_success_count = 200, guarded_success_count = 200, giving n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test returned p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.00, 0.00]. These exact numbers are drawn from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv) and the analysis log.
sections.discussion: Statistical and design interpretation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the paired design isolates validator/repair utility because both conditions begin from the same sampled candidate; therefore any paired improvement must arise from deterministic downstream repair. The observed ceiling (baseline = 1.0) invalidates the preregistered power assumptions that required non-degenerate baseline variability (target detection = 0.10). With no validator rejections there was no opportunity for repair to change final validity, so the confirmatory test is uninformative for the preregistered effect size. Root causes evidenced in the archive. The execution artifacts suggest three artifact-grounded determinants of the ceiling outcome: (i) the deterministic task generator produced candidates that satisfied the validator's mechanistic intent-constraint checks for the sampled seeds (task_payloads and representative validator traces show required_command_count equaling parsed_command_count and violation_count = 0 across episodes); (ii) the single-shared-sample sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) prevented observing generator sampling variability that might produce validator-rejectable draws; (iii) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic constraints but does not claim to detect semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a transparent paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) that isolated validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. For the synthetic task bank, gpt-5-mini sampled seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, the validator accepted every sampled candidate and no repairs were applied; baseline and guarded success were both 200/200. The preregistered power assumptions were therefore invalidated by the observed ceiling. This degenerate outcome is scientifically informative: it demonstrates that measuring validator coverage and repair utility in GVR flows requires preregistered mechanisms to produce measurable validator failures (fault injection), to expose model sampling variability (multi-sample draws), and to compare validator implementations and model families. We provide exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and to guide preregistered follow-ups that can estimate validator FP/FN behavior and the operational value of repairs under realistic fault prevalence and generator variability. Representative artifacts and the full archived bundle are available in the execution manifest referenced in the preregistration and archived artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json).

No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
